script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: Come in, both of you. So, you've chosen your site for the coastal erosion project. Tell me about it.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: We've gone for Pebble Bay, just north of the harbour. We looked at a few places, actually. Redcliff Point is eroding faster, by all accounts.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: And Pebble Bay isn't exactly easy to get to. There's no train, so it's two buses. But the main reason we picked it is that the geography department surveyed it every year from 2005 to 2015, so there's a decade of data we can compare our measurements with.

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: That's a very good reason. Previous data makes a huge difference. Now, your research question. You wrote: 'How is climate change affecting the coastline of the region?'

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: We thought it sounded important.

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: It is important, but it's far too broad for an eight-week project. You'd need data from dozens of sites. It's not too technical, and it's original enough, but I'd narrow it down to one stretch of cliff and one specific question.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: Maybe something like, 'How fast is the cliff at Pebble Bay retreating, and has the rate changed since 2015?'

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: Much better. So how will you actually measure that?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Well, we first thought about measuring the height of the cliff, but that doesn't really change much. The cliff gets shorter only very slowly.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: So instead, we'll use the fixed metal markers the department put in the ground back in 2005. We measure the distance from each marker to the cliff edge. If the distance is getting smaller, the cliff is retreating.

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: Exactly what I'd do. Some students look at sand or pebble size on the beach, but that tells you about the beach, not the cliff. Now, any practical problems you can foresee?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: We were worried about getting permission, because some of the cliff top is farmland.

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: The department already has an agreement with the farmer, so that's fine.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: Weather could be a problem, but we can always go another day. The real issue is the tide. The markers at the bottom of the cliff can only be reached for about two hours around low tide, so we'll have to plan every visit around the tide tables.

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: Yes, and please don't take any risks with that. Now, for background reading, have you found anything useful?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: There's a survey from the nineteen seventies that someone mentioned.

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: I'd be careful with that one. Their methods weren't very reliable. Interviews with local residents could be interesting, but they're quite subjective. What I'd really recommend is the report the local council published three years ago on coastal defences. It's got excellent maps and recent figures.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: Great, we'll get hold of it. Shall we talk about who's doing what?

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: Please do. I'd like to see a clear division of work.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Well, for the fieldwork, someone needs to contact the coastguard to tell them when we'll be on the beach. Amira, you said you'd do that?

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: Yes, I'll call them. My uncle actually works for them, so I know who to ask.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: Jack's got the better camera, so he's taking all the photographs of the cliff face.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: That's fine. And the statistics. I thought I'd do it all myself at first, but there's a lot of data, so we've agreed to split it and do the analysis together.

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: Sensible. What about the literature review?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: I was originally going to write that, but Amira's read far more of the background material than me, so she's taken it over.

script.speaker: Amira
script.text: And in return, Jack's going to produce all the maps. He's done a course on mapping software, so he's much quicker than me.

script.speaker: Dr Hale
script.text: It sounds like you've got a good balance. Send me your revised research question by Friday, and we'll meet again in two weeks.
